# A Formalization of the Syntax and Semantics of the ONNX Core Format in Rocq: A Rigorous Foundation for Execution-Safe Verification of Neural Networks

The formalization comes in two parts: The formalization of the ONNX-syntax and the formalization of the ONNX-semantics.

* The formalization of the ONNX-syntax is called the ONNX-model and is found in `ONNXConverter/theory/model.v`, which is generated by the *Protobuf-Converter*, which can be found in the folder `ProtobufConverter`.
* The formalization of the ONNX-semantics is called the ONNX-evaluator and is found in the folder `ONNXEvaluator`.
* An updated version of the [verified converter](https://github.com/verinncoq/converter) is also part of the repository. It uses both the ONNX-model and the ONNX-evaluator, and is much more trustworthy than its original release, as its system proof has been substantially improved. The new converter can be found in the folder `ONNXConverter`. 

## Build

### Using Nix (Recommended)

This project provides configuration for setting up a development environment with [Nix](https://nixos.org/). You can prepare and enter development shell with all base tools (Rocq, OCaml, Dune, opam, Python):
```bash
nix-shell
```
Otherwise, please enter the shell each time you want to work on the project!

### Initial dependencies setup (one-time)
Inside the Nix shell:
```bash
opam install . --deps-only
pip install -r requirements.txt
```
### Compilation and recompilation
Within the Nix shell:
```bash
dune build
```

## Usage

After compiling the project with `dune build`, you can run the following tools from the project root:

### Protobuf Converter
Converts Protocol Buffers definitions to an intermediate representation.
```bash
dune exec ./ProtobufConverter/runner/rocq_protobuf_runner.exe \
  ./data/onnx.modified.proto \
  ./out
```
*Arguments: input Protocol Buffers (.proto) file, output directory*

### ONNX Converter
Converts ONNX neural network models to Rocq code.
```bash
dune exec ./ONNXConverter/runner/onnx_converter_runner.exe \
  ./data/cartpole.onnx \
  ./out/cartpole.v \
  ./data/onnx.proto
```
*Arguments: input ONNX file, output Rocq file, Protocol Buffers schema*

### Differential Tests
Compares Rocq evaluation results with ONNX runtime execution.
```bash
python3 ./ONNXEvaluator/comparer/comparer.py \
  20 \
  ./data/cartpole.onnx \
  ./data/onnx.proto
```
*Arguments: number of test iterations, input ONNX file, Protocol Buffers schema*
